static_traits.name: Chen Xiuzhen
static_traits.social_status: Relationships somewhat strained by unwillingness to go out with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar psychological problems or treatment history in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, acceptable logic, tends toward over-analysis and self-criticism; emotions negative accompanied by guilt; skeptical about counseling but willing to try.

basic_info.main_problem: Because I do not like being forced to go out with others, I have always felt I am a useless friend.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings have negatively affected my self-esteem and my relationships with friends, so I decided to seek counseling.

core_beliefs: I am a useless / terrible friend
Only meeting others' expectations proves I have worth

special_situations.event: A friend invited her to a small gathering, but she did not want to go at the time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I decline others' invitations, it equals not caring about them and being an unqualified friend
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reluctantly accepting invitations, or repeatedly blaming myself and over-reflecting after declining to seek 'compensation'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have disappointed everyone; I am a bad / useless friend.

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not show up, friends will surely think I am unreliable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding verifying true views with friends, to evade possible dismissive judgments
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They surely think I am unreliable and do not care about them.

special_situations.event: A friend called for help in the middle of the night; after she accompanied them for hours, the other party thanked her many times
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Unless I do it perfectly, it does not count as real support
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Picking at my own expressions afterwards, dismissing positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may have said the wrong thing; I did not do enough.

special_situations.event: When she realizes she has not kept in touch with friends as she imagined recently
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should contact friends more frequently and join activities, otherwise it is failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets excessively high social standards for self, forcing compliance or producing strong guilt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I did not do enough; I am just a failed friend.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be accepted and valued by friends, while keeping autonomy and boundaries (not bound by obligations)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as unreliable and thus rejected, losing relationships
defense_goal: Maintains relationships and self-worth through self-criticism and raising standards
Avoiding directly verifying others' feedback to reduce the risk of being dismissed

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a 'bad friend' who may disappoint at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Demanding, easily judgmental others / friends who may dismiss her

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes her actual support for friends and invites her to see positive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously believing this positive evidence is insufficient to prove worth; if acknowledged, I would relax my demands on myself and be seen as unreliable
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying positive evidence, emphasizing possible inadequacies, responding in a cautious, reserved tone (e.g. 'I may still have said it wrong').

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to directly verify with friends their real views or feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Anticipating the other person will confirm her 'unreliable / not good enough' (projecting self-deprecating feelings onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoiding verification or changing the topic, expressing worry in a hesitant, self-doubting tone (e.g. 'they probably think that way').

manifestations: Disliking the social obligation of 'having to go'
Wavers between saying 'no' and fearing losing the relationship
outcomes: Avoids or reluctantly joins social activities, feeling drained

manifestations: Repeatedly declining invitations causes tension in relationships
Worrying others see her as unreliable and thus not daring to verify

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently evaluates oneself with 'I should contact friends/join activities more often'
Defines 'good friend' by rigid standards and blames himself accordingly

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Overly critical of own social performance, worrying about 'never being good enough'
Downplaying positive evidence and amplifying inadequacy in counseling

exception_events.target_problem: When friends extend social invitations, the client usually falls into guilt, labels himself a 'bad friend', and repeatedly over-analyzes after declining.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A few months ago one late night, a friend called for help in low mood, and the client stayed on the phone for hours accompanying her, with the friend expressing thanks multiple times; unlike before, she did not avoid it then, but steadily provided support.
exception_events.reason: Clue: different situation — the friend proactively asked for help with clear needs; different approach — focused listening and companionship; different support — the other's real-time thanks provided positive cues.

positive_force: Has at least one close friend to contact
Has empathy and companionship ability (once supported a friend for a long time late at night)
Willing to try counseling and reality testing
Able to identify and name own negative thoughts
negative_force: Rigid 'should' standards and excessively high self-demands
Cognitive distortions such as personalization, mind reading, black-and-white thinking
Avoiding directly verifying others' true feedback, reinforcing negative assumptions

target_behavior.behavior: Strong guilt triggered by social invitations and self-labeling ('I am a bad / useless friend')
antecedent: Realizing I have not contacted friends recently
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being seen as unreliable and losing relationships, internalizing the rule 'must accept / contact often to count as a good friend'
target_behavior.function: Avoids rejection and guilt, constraining self through self-blame and high standards or reluctantly agreeing

target_behavior.behavior: Over-analyzes social situations (repeatedly recalls, criticizes one's own expression)
antecedent: Still reviewing details after supporting a friend
target_behavior.core_reason: Insecurity about self-worth and perfectionist standards leading to extremely low tolerance for mistakes
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain a sense of control through rumination and avoid future mistakes
target_behavior.consequence: Increased anxiety and guilt, draining energy, further avoiding socializing
